summary: Latanoprost is a prostaglandin F2-alpha analog ophthalmic solution (0.005%, 50 mcg/mL) used to reduce elevated intraocular pressure in patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension. The recommended regimen is one drop in the affected eye(s) once daily in the evening, and dosing should not exceed once daily because more frequent use can reduce or paradoxically increase IOP. IOP reduction begins about 3-4 hours after a dose, peaks at 8-12 hours, and persists for at least 24 hours. The drug can cause gradual, often permanent increased brown iris pigmentation, as well as periorbital/eyelid skin darkening and eyelash changes (increased length, thickness, and number). It should be used with caution in patients with intraocular inflammation, risk factors for macular edema, or a history of herpetic keratitis, and contact lenses must be removed before instillation because of the benzalkonium chloride preservative.
indications: Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with open-angle glaucoma
Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with ocular hypertension

dosage.d: One drop (approximately 1.5 mcg) of 0.005% solution in the affected eye(s)
dosage.n: Do not exceed once daily; more frequent dosing may reduce or paradoxically increase IOP

dosage.c: Concomitant use with other topical ocular IOP-lowering drugs
dosage.d: One drop in the affected eye(s)
dosage.n: Separate different topical eye drops by at least 5 minutes; precipitation occurs if mixed with thimerosal-containing drops
Do not combine two or more prostaglandins or prostaglandin analogs

admin: Instill one drop in the affected eye(s) once daily in the evening; do not exceed once daily
Remove contact lenses before instillation; they may be reinserted 15 minutes after administration (benzalkonium chloride may be absorbed by lenses)
If more than one topical ophthalmic product is used, administer the drugs at least 5 minutes apart
Do not let the dropper tip touch the eye, eyelids, or any surface to avoid contamination and ocular infection
Avoid mixing with eye drops containing thimerosal (precipitation occurs)
Optional: nasolacrimal occlusion or gentle eyelid closure after instillation may limit systemic absorption
moa: Latanoprost is an isopropyl ester prodrug of a prostaglandin F2-alpha analog. After topical instillation it is absorbed through the cornea, where esterases hydrolyze it to the biologically active acid form. The active acid lowers intraocular pressure mainly by increasing uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humor (with a lesser effect on trabecular outflow). Because elevated IOP is a major risk factor for glaucomatous optic nerve damage and visual field loss, reducing IOP slows the likelihood of progressive injury.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to latanoprost, benzalkonium chloride, or any component of the product
relative: Active intraocular inflammation (iritis/uveitis) - generally should not be used
Active herpes simplex keratitis - should be avoided
History of intraocular inflammation (iritis/uveitis) - use with caution
History of herpetic keratitis - use with caution
Aphakia, pseudophakia with torn posterior lens capsule, or other risk factors for macular edema - use with caution

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. In animal reproduction studies, intravenous latanoprost in pregnant rabbits and rats during organogenesis produced malformations (e.g., spina bifida, cleft palate), embryofetal lethality, and spontaneous abortion at clinically relevant doses. The U.S. general-population background risk of major birth defects is 2-4% and of miscarriage is 15-20%. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit clearly justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether latanoprost or its metabolites are excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk, exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman. Weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding and the mother's clinical need for the drug against any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is provided for renal impairment with topical ocular use. Systemic absorption from one ophthalmic drop is minimal; the active acid is cleared rapidly from plasma (t1/2 about 17 minutes) and metabolites are eliminated mainly via the kidneys.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is provided for hepatic impairment with topical ocular use. The small fraction of active acid reaching the systemic circulation is primarily metabolized by the liver via fatty-acid beta-oxidation, but systemic exposure from ophthalmic dosing is minimal.

major: Other prostaglandins or prostaglandin analogs - combined use is not recommended; may reduce IOP-lowering effect or cause paradoxical IOP elevation
moderate: Eye drops containing thimerosal - precipitation occurs when mixed with latanoprost; separate instillation by at least 5 minutes
minor: Other topical ocular IOP-lowering agents - may be used concomitantly; separate by at least 5 minutes
interactions.food: Not applicable - topical ocular medication; no food interaction.
interactions.alcohol: No relevant interaction with topical ocular dosing.
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically significant laboratory test interference reported.

serious: Eyelash and vellus hair changes (length, thickness, number, misdirected growth)
Macular edema, including cystoid macular edema
Deepening of the eyelid sulcus (periorbital fat atrophy)
emergency: Severe bacterial keratitis with vision loss

monitoring: Intraocular pressure to assess therapeutic response
Iris color and periorbital/eyelid pigmentation (examine regularly if increased iris pigmentation develops)
Macular/cystoid macular edema, especially in aphakic/pseudophakic or at-risk patients
Ocular surface integrity in patients with herpetic keratitis history
counsel: Use one drop in the affected eye(s) once daily in the evening; never use more than once a day
Your eye color may gradually turn more brown; this iris color change is usually permanent even after stopping the drug
Your eyelids may darken and your eyelashes may grow longer, thicker, darker, or more numerous; eyelid and eyelash changes are usually reversible after stopping
The skin around the eye may sink in slightly (periorbital fat loss) - report noticeable changes to your doctor
Remove contact lenses before using the drops and wait 15 minutes before putting them back in
If you use more than one type of eye drop, wait at least 5 minutes between them
Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye or any surface to avoid contamination and infection
Tell your doctor right away if you develop eye pain, redness, swelling, vision changes, eye injury, infection, or have eye surgery
If you miss a dose, just take the next dose as usual - do not double up
pk: IOP reduction starts about 3-4 hours after a dose
Maximum IOP-lowering effect at 8-12 hours; aqueous humor peak about 2 hours after instillation
Active acid plasma t1/2 approximately 17 minutes
IOP reduction present for at least 24 hours
Store unopened bottle refrigerated at 2-8 C; protect from light; after opening may be kept at room temperature up to 25 C for 6 weeks
pearls: Dose in the evening; once-daily dosing is optimal - more frequent use can reduce or paradoxically raise IOP
Increased brown iris pigmentation is typically permanent, while eyelid darkening and eyelash changes are usually reversible after discontinuation
Watch for deepening of the eyelid sulcus from periorbital fat atrophy, especially with unilateral therapy causing asymmetry
Avoid in active intraocular inflammation or active herpes simplex keratitis; use caution with macular-edema risk factors (aphakia, torn posterior capsule)
Remove contact lenses before instillation due to benzalkonium chloride; reinsert after 15 minutes
IOP reduction is equivalent to timolol 0.5% twice daily but achieved with once-daily dosing
missed: If a dose is missed, do not double up - simply continue treatment with the next scheduled evening dose as normal.
overdose: Ocular overdose (more than one drop) is treated symptomatically; there is no specific antidote. Systemic absorption from topical use is minimal. In studies, IV latanoprost up to 3 mcg/kg produced no adverse reactions, while higher IV doses (5.5-10 mcg/kg) caused abdominal pain, dizziness, fatigue, hot flushes, nausea, and sweating. Provide supportive, symptomatic care.
